extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom designers, and journalism students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing infographics, charts, and interactive graphics in news reporting — how to choose forms, tools, and practices so visual storytelling makes complex information clear, credible, and engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of infographics / simplify complex information
rubrics_metrics.description: Infographics stand out as a lively and interesting way to tell a story by taking difficult data and making it look good and easy to understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short writing, pictures, and graphs to keep people interested; present facts in the form of a story so readers can understand and remember them better; treat infographics as the bridge between raw data and audience understanding. Anti-patterns: long dense text, overly complex visuals that don't summarize the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use statistics to provide quantitative basis and credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics give stories a quantitative basis and boost the trustworthiness of news stories by showing trends, backing up arguments, and finding patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct interpretation of data; when in doubt, seek expert statistical help or collaboration (the page mentions 'statistic assignment help') to analyze data correctly. Journalists must make sure their numeric interpretations fit the broader story. Anti-patterns: using statistics without verification or context, misinterpreting correlations as causation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose appropriate chart types for the data
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick the right chart style for the data before turning it into insights (e.g., pie chart for amounts/proportions, line graph for changes over time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match chart form to the data and the story you want to tell so visuals explain rather than obscure. Consider audience attention spans and use charts that make difficult numbers easier to understand. Anti-patterns: using a decorative or trendy chart type that conceals the message; swapping chart types arbitrarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design interactive graphics to engage and inform
rubrics_metrics.description: Interactive graphics change how people get information by allowing users to zoom, change views, and explore — turning reading into an engaging experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make interactivity purposeful: enable exploration that deepens understanding, supports retention, and increases participation. Ensure interactions are usable and meaningful (e.g., filters, zoom, alternate views). Anti-patterns: gimmicky interactions that add no insight or confuse users; heavy interactions that break accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select data-visualization tools based on skill, style, and story complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Different tools have trade-offs; choose based on ability level and the complexity of the infographic (Canva for templates and ease, Piktochart for drag-and-drop styling, Adobe Illustrator for complex, custom design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh pros and cons: ease-of-use vs. customization vs. professional control. Newcomers may prefer template-driven tools; experienced designers may prefer vector/design tools for bespoke visuals. Anti-patterns: forcing a story into a tool that can't represent its complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach data visualization in journalism education
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism programs should teach data representation alongside writing to prepare students for a picture-based, digital news environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both technical skills (charts, tools, interactivity) and lessons in flexible thinking about how visuals and storytelling intersect. Prepare students to navigate the blurred lines between traditional and digital media. Implementation note: combine practical tool training with principles of clarity and ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize accuracy, fairness, and transparency with data
rubrics_metrics.description: When working with large or complex datasets, ensuring correctness, fairness, and transparency is an ongoing issue requiring care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vet sources, document methods, disclose limitations, and avoid misleading representations; treat ethical concerns (bias, omissions) as central. Anti-patterns: hiding caveats, cherry-picking data, or producing visuals that mislead to create a stronger narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate visuals with narrative writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrating data visualization with writing creates a more powerful way to tell stories; each element (infographic, chart, interactive) plays a role in communicating information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design visuals to complement and enhance the written story rather than replace it; continue learning new techniques and trends so visuals and prose work together to keep readers informed and engaged. Practical tip: plan narrative and visuals together from the reporting stage.
